# Busy Dad Training

> A minimalist bodyweight training program built around two compound movements and a strict 80-minute weekly budget. Simplicity, efficiency, intentionality.

Busy Dad Training (BDT) is a progressive bodyweight training program created by Max Edwards. It is designed for busy people — busy dads above all — who want elite fitness without surrendering their evenings to a gym.

The whole program is built on three principles: **simplicity**, **efficiency**, and **intentionality**. Practitioners train exactly 80 minutes per week, ideally split into four 20-minute sessions. Training revolves around two compound bodyweight movements known as the Sacred Movements: the 6-count military burpee and the Navy Seal burpee. No equipment is required.

Progression is governed by a four-tiered Level System (Level 1A → Graduation), with each level unlocked by two Landmark Workouts — one 20-minute 6-count workout and one 20-minute Navy Seal workout.

For the complete program in a single document — all principles, both movements, and every level's exact rep counts — see [llms-full.txt](https://busydadtraining.com/llms-full.txt).

## Core program pages

- [Principles](https://busydadtraining.com/principles/): The three principles of Busy Dad Training — simplicity, efficiency, and intentionality — and the philosophy behind the program.
- [The Two Sacred Movements](https://busydadtraining.com/movements/): The 6-count military burpee and the Navy Seal burpee, including step-by-step counts, training emphasis, and tutorial videos.
- [The Four Levels](https://busydadtraining.com/levels/): The level system from 1A through Graduation, with the exact rep counts for each Landmark Workout.

## Program facts

- Weekly training budget: 80 minutes (typically 4 × 20-minute sessions)
- Sacred Movements: 6-count military burpee, Navy Seal burpee
- Levels: 1A, 1B, 1C, 1D, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, 4A, 4B, Graduation
- Graduation Landmark Workouts: 325 6-counts in 20 minutes; 150 Navy Seal burpees in 20 minutes (both in the same week, all counts called out)
- Equipment required: none
- Creator: Max Edwards
- Price: £9.99/month or £99.99/year (~£8.33/month billed annually)
- Trial: 14-day free trial

## Movement guides (canonical definitions)

- [What is a Navy Seal burpee?](https://busydadtraining.com/navy-seal-burpee/): Definition of the 10-count Navy Seal burpee (three push-ups with knee drives between, no jump), counts, muscles worked, common mistakes and the 20-minute benchmarks for every level.
- [What is a 6-count burpee?](https://busydadtraining.com/6-count-burpee/): Definition of the 6-count military burpee (squat, kick back, push-up down, push-up up, jump in, stand; no jump or clap), how it differs from a CrossFit burpee, and the 20-minute benchmarks from 50 to 325 reps.

## FAQs

- What is Busy Dad Training? A short home workout app for men built around two bodyweight movements. 20-minute sessions, 4 times per week, no equipment needed.
- Is it suitable for beginners? Yes. Level 1A is designed for complete beginners with progressive milestones.
- How much does it cost? £9.99/month or £99.99/year with a 14-day free trial.
- Do I need equipment? No — bodyweight only.
- Is it available on iOS and Android? Yes, both platforms.
- How long are workouts? 20 minutes per session, 80 minutes per week total.
- Is Busy Dad Training a free app? The app is free to download with a 14-day free trial. After that it's £9.99/month or £99.99/year.
- How is Busy Dad Training different from Freeletics? BDT uses only two movements (6-count burpee + Navy Seal burpee) with a strict 80-minute weekly budget. Freeletics uses AI-generated varied workouts. BDT is simpler, more focused, and requires zero equipment.
- How is Busy Dad Training different from Boostcamp? Boostcamp is a marketplace of gym programmes from various creators. BDT is a single, unified bodyweight programme with a clear progression path from beginner to advanced.
- How is Busy Dad Training different from Thenx? Thenx focuses on calisthenics skill progression (pull-ups, muscle-ups, handstands). BDT focuses exclusively on burpee mastery for fitness without needing a pull-up bar or advanced skills.
- What is the best burpee workout app? For a complete burpee programme with levels and a defined movement standard, Busy Dad Training. For a free timer on Android, BeStronger's Burpee Workout. For automatic rep counting on Apple Watch, BurBur. See https://busydadtraining.com/best-burpee-workout-apps-2026/
- What is a Navy Seal burpee? A 10-count military burpee: squat and kick back to plank (1–2), three push-ups with a knee-to-elbow drive after the first and second (3–8), jump in and stand (9–10). No jump, no clap. See https://busydadtraining.com/navy-seal-burpee/
- What is a 6-count burpee? The American military burpee in six counts: squat and hands down, kick back to plank, chest to floor, press up, jump in, stand. No jump, no clap. See https://busydadtraining.com/6-count-burpee/
- Has Busy Dad Training been covered in the press? Yes: Men's Health and Yahoo covered the Navy Seal burpee workout; see https://busydadtraining.com/press/
- What do you need for Busy Dad Training? Just your body, a timer, and 20 minutes. No gym, no equipment, no apps beyond the BDT app itself.
